methods.label: Factor and compare signs
methods.explanation:
Moving everything to one side lets us determine when a product is negative:
\[
2x^2+x-6=(2x-3)(x+2)<0.
\]
The corresponding boundary equation has roots \(-2\) and \(\frac32\). A product is negative precisely when its factors have opposite signs.

If \(x<-2\), both factors are negative, so their product is positive. If \(-2<x<\frac32\), then \(2x-3<0\) and \(x+2>0\), so the product is negative. If \(x>\frac32\), both factors are positive.

At either boundary the product is zero, which does not satisfy the strict inequality. Therefore the complete solution is \(\boxed{-2<x<\frac32}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
